_comment: EXAMPLE ONLY. Replace every entry with the queries the realm under test
actually issues, transcribed from its card source. The shapes here are
invented placeholders that match no real realm.
Queries are written in the `_federated-search` ENTRY wire grammar: the
type anchor is `item.on`, and field paths inside eq/contains/in/range
carry an `item.` prefix. `${realm}` expands to the realm URL under test.
Every key other than `label` is sent to the endpoint as-is, so `sort` and
`page` work here too, and a filter is passed through whole — see the
predicates in extraQueries below, which is how a run A/Bs adding one to a
query that has none. See lib/workload.ts.
`fieldset` selects which document the searches ask for, and so which code
path the run measures: `item` is card data only, the path a query-backed
field takes; `entries` (the default) is the prerendered renderings a grid
fetches, and costs several times as much for the same filter. A single
query can carry its own `fields` member instead, which wins for itself —
that is how one workload models a screen whose surfaces differ.
`variants` are the filter fragments a shape cycles through, one per
re-run, merged over its own filter. Without them a shape asks the same
question every time and the realm answers it from its live-search cache
after the first, so the run reports what a cache hit costs rather than
what answering costs. Pick values that match rows: a fragment selecting
nothing is a cheap search that measures none of the shape's work.
`writes` names one block per kind of write, and writer slots take them in
order. Two blocks pinned to two usernames put two identities on one realm,
which is the only shape in which the per-realm indexing lane is visible
from outside — a single block cannot produce it however many writers run
it. The PATCH block below is the expensive half: patching a card that many
instances link to invalidates all of them, while a POST creates a card
nothing links to yet and its pass visits one file. Differing `everyMs`
cadences are what give the run both halves of the reading, cheap writes
that land inside an expensive pass and cheap writes that do not. Grant the
second account write access first: setup-realm.ts --write-grants 1.
